subject: general
question: A sphere has a radius of 8 cm. A solid cylinder has a base radius of 4 cm and a height of h cm. If the total surface area of the cylinder is half the surface area of the sphere, then find the height of the cylinder.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Surface area of the sphere = 4πR² = 4 × π × 8² = 256π cm²

Total surface area (TSA) of the cylinder = 1/2 × 256π = 128π cm²

Using the formula TSA of cylinder = 2πr(r + h) where r = 4 cm:

⇒ 2 × π × 4 × (4 + h) = 128π

⇒ 8π(4 + h) = 128π ⇒ 4 + h = 16 ⇒ h = 12

**∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of sphere (R) = 8 cm

Base radius of solid cylinder (r) = 4 cm

Total Surface Area of cylinder = 1/2 × Surface Area of sphere

 
 
 

 

 
• 
 
 R = 8 cm
 
 
 
 
 

 

 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 
 
 
• 
 r = 4 cm
 
 
 
• 
 

 

 h = ?
 
 
 TSA (Cylinder) = 1/2 × SA (Sphere)

**Formula Used:**

Surface Area of sphere = 4 × π × R²

Total Surface Area of solid cylinder = 2 × π × r × (r + h)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Surface Area of sphere = 4 × π × (8)²

⇒ Surface Area of sphere = 4 × π × 64 = 256π cm²

⇒ Total Surface Area of cylinder = 1/2 × 256π = 128π cm²

⇒ 2 × π × r × (r + h) = 128π

⇒ 2 × π × 4 × (4 + h) = 128π

⇒ 8π × (4 + h) = 128π

⇒ 4 + h = 128π ÷ 8π

⇒ 4 + h = 16

⇒ h = 16 − 4 = 12 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cylinder Area & Volume

Curved Surface Area = 2πrh, Total Surface Area = 2πr(r + h), Volume = πr²h

Sphere Area & Volume

Surface Area = 4πR², Volume = (4/3)πR³

Hemisphere Area & Volume

Curved Surface Area = 2πR², Total Surface Area = 3πR², Volume = (2/3)πR³
